views.markdown:
Shows one signed number and an estimated time beside the iPad status bar battery percentage. The label uses the stock status bar font and colour.

**+** means energy is going into the battery. **-** means the battery is powering the iPad.

The value is **net battery power in watts**, calculated from battery current and voltage. It is not the charger's advertised wattage: the charger first runs the iPad, and the number is what is left over for the battery.

`+6.2W 3h30m  26%  [battery]`
`-3.1W 1h07m  12%  [battery]`

- `+6.2W` — charging at about 6.2 W into the battery
- `3h30m` — estimated time until full
- `-3.1W` — draining at about 3.1 W
- `1h07m` — estimated time until empty
- `0W` — full on power, or negligible flow

When draining, the estimate prefers iOS's own time-remaining value and falls back to remaining mAh ÷ current. When charging, it projects the remaining capacity at the current net charge rate, so it changes as charging tapers. These are estimates, not promises.

**iPad only.** iPadOS 15 or later, rootless jailbreak. To make room, the status icons immediately left of the battery percentage are shifted left by the exact width of the rate and time; the shift updates when the text or icons change.
